messages.subject: rmr - Package running error
parts:
I am new in R and hadoop,
When i running this below R codes I used to getting error like this.
Can anyone tell me how to set the env variable. I have tried lot.
> library(rmr2)
> from.dfs(
+   mapreduce(
+     input = to.dfs(row.names(mtcars)),
+     map = function(.,words) 
+       keyval(unlist(strsplit(words,'\\s+')),1),
+     reduce = function(word, count) 
+       keyval(word, sum(count)),
+     backend.parameters = list(hadoop=list(D="mapred.reduce.tasks=1"))
+   )
+ )
Error in hadoop.streaming() : 
  Please make sure that the env. variable HADOOP_STREAMING or HADOOP_HOME are set
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In mapreduce(input = to.dfs(row.names(mtcars)), map = function(.,  :
  backend.parameters is deprecated.
2: In to.dfs(row.names(mtcars)) :
  Converting to.dfs argument to keyval with a NULL key

messages.author: 6ac7e7dfbe4f6c38
messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#803] rmr - Package running error
parts:
Hi Kokila,
 the best approach would be to get to know the Unix shell. There's plenty of books but the way I did it was

man bash

and read for three hours. That said if you insist on using something without understanding it, enter 

export HADOOP_STREAMING=<path-to-streaming>
export HADOOP_CMD=`which hadoop`

at the shell prompt. To state the obvious,  <path-to-streaming> is not to be taken literally. You need to find the streaming jar whose location changes from distribution to distribution and installation to installation, so I don't know exactly where it is in your case. This command could be helpful

find . -name hadoop-streaming\*jar 2>/dev/null

If you have a single line of output, that's probably it. If you have multiple ones, you probably have multiple versions of hadoop installed. If you have none, you probably haven't installed hadoop yet. I hope this gets you going


Antonio
